record.paper_title: Towards Knowledge Exchange: State-of-the-Art and Open Problems
record.original_question: How can researchers create shared open-source real-world scenarios and corpora for knowledge translation and exchange so that knowledge-base mapping generation tools can be evaluated comparably, including evaluation of ranking measures when several mappings are structurally consistent but differ in intended semantics?

evidence.quote: Currently there are not enough open source real world scenarios that can be used for settings which involve KBs.
We believe knowledge translation and exchange research can greatly benefit from a community effort which identifies corpora that can be shared to produce comparable evaluations of KGMT.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the problem of evaluating tools that automatically generate mappings between knowledge bases (KBs). A knowledge base is a structured collection of entities, relations, and axioms (for example, an ontology together with assertional data). Given two knowledge bases K_1 and K_2, a mapping M is a set of correspondences between elements of K_1 and elements of K_2; M is said to be structurally consistent if it preserves the schema-level constraints (such as class hierarchies and domain/range restrictions) of both K_1 and K_2. Different mappings may be structurally consistent yet correspond to different intended semantics.

Design a methodology for the comparative evaluation of knowledge-base mapping generation tools that achieves all of the following:

(a) Specify a collection of shared, open, real-world scenarios and corpora (pairs of knowledge bases together with reference mappings or ground-truth semantic annotations) suitable for benchmarking knowledge translation and exchange tasks.

(b) Define quantitative evaluation measures that, given a candidate mapping M produced by a tool, score both its structural consistency and its agreement with intended semantics.

(c) Provide ranking measures capable of distinguishing among multiple candidate mappings that are all structurally consistent but differ in their intended semantics, and prove or argue that the ranking measures satisfy reasonable axioms (such as monotonicity with respect to semantic agreement and invariance under irrelevant transformations of the KBs).

The goal is to produce a framework under which different mapping generation tools can be compared in a reproducible and semantically meaningful way.
artifact.status_search_result: This is a community-level research challenge concerning the creation of shared benchmarks and ranking measures for knowledge-base mapping evaluation. While initiatives such as the Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative (OAEI) provide partial benchmarks, no comprehensive solution covering real-world KB translation scenarios and semantically-aware ranking of structurally consistent mappings has been established. The problem remains open as a community effort.

status_evidence.title: Ontology Alignment Evaluation Initiative
status_evidence.snippet: OAEI organizes annual evaluation campaigns for ontology matching but acknowledges limitations in real-world KB scenarios and semantic ranking.
status_evidence.claim: Existing benchmarks partially address structural mapping evaluation but do not fully resolve ranking by intended semantics.
